content.Indication: In suspected phenotypes requiring specific treatments (i.e. giant cell myocarditis, eosinophilic myocarditis, sarcoidosis, vasculitis, SLE, other systemic auto-immune inflammatory conditions, or storage diseases).
content.Number_of_samples: A minimum of 5 but possibly at least 7 samples: 3 for pathology, 2 for infection (DNA, PCR) and 2 for RNA viruses/viral replication.
content.Aetiology: Search for common cardiotrophic viruses (parvovirus B19, HHV4, HHV6, enteroviruses, adenovirus and coxsackie) by quantitative rtPCR when a viral aetiology is suspected. Viral mRNA for active viral replication should be assessed, if possible.
content.Further_assessment_if_indicated: CMV, HIV, Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme disease), Coxiella burnetii (Q-fever), Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas disease) and SARS-CoV-2.
content.Immunohistochemistry: Quantification of CD3-, CD4-, CD8- or CD45- staining lymphocytes and CD68 macrophages per mm2; anti-HLA-DR.
content.Histology: Haematoxylin and eosin staining, fibrosis assessment with Masson's Trichrome and Picrosirius Red, amyloid fibrils detection with Congo Red.
content.Therapeutic_options: HF treatment for HFrEF per guideline sections. Consider disease-specific therapies: Lyme disease treated with doxycycline; Chagas disease treated according to recommendations. Consider immunosuppressive therapy in giant cell myocarditis, eosinophilic myocarditis, sarcoidosis or vasculitis and in selected patients with increased cardiac inflammation.
content.Genetic_considerations: LMNA, RBM20, PLN and FLN mutation: higher risk of sudden cardiac death; consider early indication for primary prevention by ICD implantation guided by risk factors. TTN mutation: higher rate of LV reverse remodeling (in up to 70%), but higher risk of atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
content.Diagnostic_criteria_and_definitions: DCM: LV dilatation and systolic dysfunction in absence of known abnormal loading conditions or significant CAD. HNDC: LV or biventricular global systolic dysfunction (LVEF <45%) without dilatation in absence of known abnormal loading conditions or significant CAD. Familial criteria: two or more first- or second-degree relatives with DCM or HNDC, or a first-degree relative with autopsy-proven DCM and sudden death at <50 years of age.
